title: AKSHAR ruler ground truth
description: One row per photograph of the sealed test split. Describes the CSV at data/test_split/ground_truth.csv, whose columns are these properties in this order. Tracked in git although the CSV itself is not, so the shape of the set survives where the set does not.

filename.description: Path to the frame, relative to data/test_split/. Exactly two per packet: the pair is what separates our own repeatability from ruler error.

product.description: What the packet is. Grouped with pack_size, never alone: section 10 treats 30 g and 100 g of one product as different SKUs with different height thresholds, and averaging their shots together would repeat that mistake in the scoring.

pack_size.description: Declared net quantity as printed, e.g. '300ml'. Empty where the pack declares none, as on a matchbox or a single unit.

field.description: Which declaration was measured. u1_report matches this against Declaration.field, so a value the pipeline never emits scores as unmeasured rather than as an error.

character.description: The specific glyph the rule was laid against, where it was recorded. Optional and often empty. Cap height, x-height and full text height differ by a third on the same line, so where this is empty the comparison rests on the assumption that a cap height was read — check u1_report's systematic bias before trusting the MAE.

measured_mm.description: Height in millimetres as read from a steel rule. The resolution of this number bounds the accuracy that can be demonstrated: a value rounded to the nearest millimetre carries up to 0.5 mm of its own error, against a U1 target of 0.15 mm.

notes.description: Free text. Carries the photographer's original folder name verbatim, so the parse in scripts/seal_test_split.py can be checked by eye.
